chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: Claude Thornhill's choice of 'Loch Lomond' and 'Annie Laurie'
summary: Claude selected the folk songs; they expected 'Annie Laurie' to be the hit, and she had not sung either in Pittsburgh.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So I think that Claude -- Well at the time, the reason that Claude selected 'Lock Lomond' was because --
We felt that 'Annie Laurie' might make the hit. We had no idea that 'Lock Lomond' would do anything.
Can I ask you this? We'll come back, as I say, in the next interview to the Pittsburgh period of your life and so on, but did you sing either of those songs in Pittsburgh before you came to New York?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

No. My big song in Pittsburgh -- that is, getting into the swing and the classy bit was "Trees". But we never recorded that.

You see, when I came to New York -- let's face it, you had a whole lot of singers here already. I think Claude was sort of wise to select these things like "Loch Lomond" and "Annie Laurie" -- was that at least make it a little different from just an average vocalist (singing) in front of the band.

And it isn't a novelty. Claude may have known what he was doing, because I knew from nothing -- I just went along for the ride.
So he really was responsible for decisions to use that material?
